w:r.w:t: Bias-Resilient Meeting Onboarding – Core 4-Minute Assessment
Purpose: Power first-meeting coaching with the smallest set of high-yield signals. Tone: plain language, non-clinical. No diagnostic intent.
Instructions: Answer quickly and honestly. Use confidence sliders where shown. Completion time about 4 minutes.
1) Cognitive Reflection, Numeracy, and Calibration
Answer and give your confidence 0 to 100 percent.
1. A tool and a case cost 110 dollars in total. The tool costs 100 dollars more than the case. How much does the case cost? __
Confidence 0 to 100 percent: __
2. It takes five machines five minutes to make five widgets. How long would it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets? __ minutes
Confidence 0 to 100 percent: __
3. A fair six-sided die will be rolled once. Which is more likely: a number greater than 4, or an even number? Choose one: Greater than 4 | Even number
Confidence 0 to 100 percent: __
4. A company’s revenue grew from 40 million to 44 million year over year. What is the percentage growth, to the nearest whole percent? __ percent
Confidence 0 to 100 percent: __
5. Prediction interval: Give a 90 percent confidence range for the average height of adult men in your country. From __ to __ (units shown in app).
2) Actively Open-Minded Thinking
Rate 1 to 5.
1. I look for reasons why I might be wrong.
2. I change my mind when new information is strong.
3. I like to hear the best case for views I disagree with.
4. I consider alternative explanations before I decide.
5. I ask clarifying questions when I disagree.
3) Need for Closure and Ambiguity Tolerance
Rate 1 to 5.
1. I prefer quick decisions even when some facts are missing.
2. Unclear instructions make me uncomfortable.
3. I am patient when problems have no single right answer. (reverse)
4. I am fine delaying a choice to gather more evidence. (reverse)
4) Current State Check and Attention
1. Mood right now: Very negative 1 2 3 4 5 Very positive
2. Stress right now: Very low 1 2 3 4 5 Very high
3. Mental effort available for this meeting: Very low 1 2 3 4 5 Very high
4. Attention check: Please select option 2 here. 1 2 3 4 5
5) Intent Attribution Vignette
A teammate shares a document with several comments that question your approach and sends it late at night with no greeting. What is your first interpretation?
Choose one: a) They are trying to help improve the work. b) They are frustrated with me. c) They want more context. d) They do not respect my time.
Confidence 0 to 100 percent: __
6) Anchoring Micro-game
A colleague suggests 400 dollars as a monthly budget ceiling.
What is your independent best budget after thinking for 10 seconds? __ dollars
7) Data Quality Items
Attention check: To show you are reading, select option 4 here. 1 2 3 4 5
Impression balance: I always treat people with complete respect, even when I am very stressed. 1 2 3 4 5
Engineering Scoring and Nudge Rules
• Calibration and numeracy: Compute percent-correct for the four scored items (tool/case, widgets, die, percent growth). Compute confidence-accuracy gap = average confidence
minus percent-correct*100. If gap > 20, flag calibration gap. If user answers 0–1 of 4 correctly, enable offer ranges and invite counter-examples.
• Prediction interval: If 90 percent range width is extremely wide (e.g., > 2.5 SDs of typical width) or empty, down-weight interval for calibration scoring.
• Actively open-minded thinking: Average the five items (1–5). If mean < 3.0, turn on ask one clarifying question before asserting. If mean > 4.0, reduce interruptive nudges.

• Need for closure: Reverse the two reverse-keyed items. Average the four items. If mean > 4.0, enable seek one more perspective when time-to-decision < 5 minutes. If mean < 2.5, suppress those prompts.
• State check: If mood ≤ 2, stress ≥ 4, or effort ≤ 2, increase caution on tone and attribution in the first 10 minutes.
• Intent attribution: If user selects hostile options (b or d) with confidence ≥ 70, enable benefit-of-the-doubt prompts and request one example before concluding.
• Anchoring: Anchor is 400. If independent estimate is within ±10 percent of 400 and calibration gap is flagged, raise reminders to form independent estimates before hearing anchors.

• Validity: If either attention check is failed, flag low data quality and soften score certainty. If impression item is 5 and many Agree items are 5 with very fast response times, down-weight Agree-keyed items.
